title: Embarrassed on someone else’s behalf
odia: ନାଚିଲା ଲୋକକୁ ଲାଜ ନାହିଁ ଦେଖିଲା ଲୋକକୁ ଲାଜ
literal_meaning: The person dancing feels no embarrassment; the person watching does.
explanation: The dictionary explains a mismatch: someone behaves without embarrassment while witnesses feel ashamed on that person’s behalf. The saying can name that uncomfortable distance between an action and how it appears to others. Its image need not be used to condemn dancing or to police someone’s harmless enjoyment.
meaning_odia: ଯେଉଁ ଲୋକ କାମଟି କରୁଛି, ତାକୁ ଲାଜ ଲାଗୁନାହିଁ; ଦେଖୁଥିବା ଲୋକ ତା ପାଇଁ ଅସହଜ ହେଉଛି। ନିଜ ଆଚରଣ ଅନ୍ୟଙ୍କୁ କିପରି ଲାଗୁଛି, ସେଥିପ୍ରତି ଅସଚେତନ ରହିଲେ ଏଭଳି ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ହୋଇପାରେ। ଏଠି ନାଚର ଚିତ୍ର ଅଛି ବୋଲି ନାଚିବାକୁ ଲଜ୍ଜାର କାମ ଭାବିବା ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ।
english_summary: The dictionary explains a mismatch: someone behaves without embarrassment while witnesses feel ashamed on that person’s behalf.
odia_summary: ଯେଉଁ ଲୋକ କାମଟି କରୁଛି, ତାକୁ ଲାଜ ଲାଗୁନାହିଁ; ଦେଖୁଥିବା ଲୋକ ତା ପାଇଁ ଅସହଜ ହେଉଛି।
usage_example: Someone loudly claims credit for a group effort while their companions exchange embarrassed looks. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The dictionary explicitly labels the entry a proverb and gives this social-use gloss. Its alternative scatological wording is not needed for this candidate.

title: A boat needs a river
literal_meaning: What can a boat do when the river dries up?
explanation: A useful boat cannot replace the water it needs. The image invites a distinction between ability and the conditions that make ability useful. When an essential resource disappears, blaming the tool or the person alone may miss the real obstacle. This wider application is an editorial interpretation of the quoted saying.
meaning_odia: ନାଆ ଭଲ ଥିଲେ ବି ଶୁଖିଲା ନଈରେ ଚାଲିପାରିବ ନାହିଁ। କାମ କରିବାର କ୍ଷମତା ସହ ସେଥିପାଇଁ ଦରକାରୀ ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ମଧ୍ୟ ରହିବା ଦରକାର। ମୂଳ ସାଧନଟି ନଥିଲେ କେବଳ ଲୋକ ବା ଯନ୍ତ୍ରକୁ ଦୋଷ ଦେଇ ସମସ୍ୟା ବୁଝିହେବ ନାହିଁ—ନଈ ଓ ନାଆର ଚିତ୍ରରୁ ଏହି ବିଚାରଟି ଆସେ।
english_summary: A useful boat cannot replace the water it needs.

odia: ପରଧନେ ଲହର ଫହର; ଛଡାଇ ନେଲେ ଲାଜେ ମର
title: A flourish on someone else’s wealth
literal_meaning: You move about in style on another’s wealth; when it is taken away, you die of shame.
explanation: The first half gives someone room to move and make a show; the second suddenly takes that support away. The dictionary defines the headword as moving to and fro, while the verse puts that movement on another person’s wealth. Read as a taunt, it catches the embarrassment of displaying what one cannot claim as one’s own. The closing “die of shame” is exaggerated reproach, not a literal instruction. Our wider reading concerns borrowed display and insecure pretension, not the worth of people who receive help.
meaning_odia: ପରର ଧନରେ ଚାଲିଛି ଲହର ଫହର; ସେ ଧନ ଫେରିଗଲେ ଦେଖାଣିର ଭିତ୍ତିଟି ମଧ୍ୟ ରହେନାହିଁ। ପ୍ରଥମ ଭାଗର ଆରାମ ଓ ଚଳପ୍ରଚଳକୁ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଭାଗର ଲାଜ ହଠାତ୍ ଅଟକାଇଦିଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ନିଜର ନୁହେଁ ଏମିତି ଜିନିଷକୁ ନିଜ ବଡ଼ପଣର ପ୍ରମାଣ କରି ଦେଖାଇବା ଏହି ଟାହିର ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ। “ଲାଜେ ମର” କଥାର ଅତିରଞ୍ଜନ; ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ନେଉଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ଛୋଟ କରିବା ଏଠାରେ ଆମର ପଢ଼ା ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: Borrowed display can become embarrassment when its support is withdrawn.
odia_summary: ପରର ଧନରେ ନିଜ ବଡ଼ପଣ ଦେଖାଇଲେ, ତାହା ଫେରିଗଲେ ଲାଜରେ ପଡ଼ିବାର ଟାହି।
usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone poses with a friend’s expensive camera and lets others think it belongs to them. When the friend asks for it back, another friend quotes the saying softly. The joke concerns the false impression, not borrowing a camera.
cultural_context: The dictionary labels the headword Sambalpur; this is a source label, not proof of exclusive regional origin. The display reading is editorial close reading, not an independently supplied traditional-use gloss.

odia: ଯାହାକୁ ଯେ ? ବିରିକି ଚାଉଳ ତିନ୍ତେଇ ଦେ
title: A fitting pair
literal_meaning: Whatever suits each: soak black gram and rice.
explanation: The entry defines the opening as what is appropriate to a person or thing. Its answer brings black gram and rice together in the action of soaking. Our reading follows the pairing: usefulness can depend on what accompanies something. The quotation names no finished dish, proportion or rule for sorting people into groups.
meaning_odia: ଆରମ୍ଭର କଥାକୁ ଅଭିଧାନ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ବା ବସ୍ତୁ ପ୍ରତି ଯାହା ଉପଯୁକ୍ତ ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ। ଉତ୍ତରରେ ବିରି ଓ ଚାଉଳ ତିନ୍ତେଇବାର କାମ ଆସେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ମେଳଟି ମୁଖ୍ୟ—ଗୋଟିଏ ଜିନିଷ ସହ କଣ ରହୁଛି, ତାହା ତାର ଉପଯୋଗକୁ ବଦଳାଇପାରେ। ଢଗଟି କୌଣସି ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତ ଖାଦ୍ୟର ନାମ, ପରିମାଣ ବା ମଣିଷକୁ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀରେ ବାଣ୍ଟିବାର ନିୟମ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
english_summary: A food pairing carries our reading about useful accompaniment.
odia_summary: ଖାଦ୍ୟର ମେଳରେ ଉପଯୋଗୀ ସଙ୍ଗତିକୁ ନେଇ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ଏକ ଶିଶୁପାଠରେ ମାନଚିତ୍ରଟି ଏକା ଦେଖି ପିଲାମାନେ ବୁଝିପାରୁନଥିଲେ। ଶିକ୍ଷକ ଛୋଟ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନାଟି ପାଖରେ ରଖି କହିଲେ, “ଏବେ ଦୁଇଟିକୁ ମିଶାଇ ପଢ଼ିବା,” ଓ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇଲେ। / Children find a map unclear on its own. A teacher places a short description beside it: “Now read the two together,” recalling the saying. This classroom use is invented.
cultural_context: The food image and explicit appropriateness gloss are retained. Complementary teaching materials are our application, not a documented traditional use or a recipe.
